rationale: Lexeme used both nominally (line 23: 'according to his ⲫⲛⲟ') and verbally (line 24: 'his upward going ⲫⲛⲟ-s inward unto him'). Possibly Lyc reflex of ⲡⲱⲛ 'transfer, pass over,' giving 'progress, transit, proceeding.' Designates the catechumen's path/transit through the cosmic stations toward purification and ascension. Confidence low; flagged for parallel attestations elsewhere in the Kephalaia.

Likely Lyc qualitative of ⲥⲱⲟⲩϩ 'gather, assemble.' Used here of the catechumen 'gathered into' the church during his lifetime — ecclesiological-incorporational sense. Distinct from but parallel to ⲥⲟⲩⲱϩ 'gather' attested elsewhere.

Compound: ⲕⲁ- (causative of ⲕⲱ 'leave, remit') + ⲛⲁⲃⲉ ('sin'). Standard Coptic confessional-religious term for 'remission, forgiveness of sins.' Here as object of the catechumen's prayer alongside ⲙⲉⲧⲁⲛⲟⲓⲁ 'repentance.'
Lycopolitan plural ⲡⲏⲛⲩⲉ = Sahidic ⲡⲏⲩⲉ 'the heavens.' Variant orthography with intrusive ⲛ. Standard cosmological term for the celestial realm to which catechumens ascend after death.
Variant of ⲡⲉϩⲍⲟ 'his face' (already in glossary) with epenthetic ⲉ-vowel. Lyc orthographic variant. Same root as ⲡⲍⲟ 'the face.'
Lycopolitan ⲡⲱⲏⲛ = Sahidic ⲡϣⲏⲛ 'tree.' Standard agricultural term in the harvest-typology where ripe fruits (= souls of catechumens) are placed upon the tree.
Likely Lyc plural of ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁ/ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲉ 'mercy, alms' — the works of charity by which catechumens participate in the soteriological economy. Modified by ⲛ̄ⲛ̄ⲕⲁⲧⲏⲭⲟⲩⲙⲉⲛⲟⲥ 'of the catechumens' in line 18-19.

Possessed substantival noun on ⲧⲁⲗⲟ 'mount, raise up' (cf. ⲧⲁⲗⲏⲩ 'be exalted/mounted' in glossary) = 'his mounting-up, his ascension.' Paired with ⲡⲉϩⲧⲟⲩⲃⲟ 'his purification' as the dyadic eschatological process for the catechumen.
Compound ⲡⲕⲉ- ('the also/other') + ⲥⲉⲡⲉ (= Lyc reflex of ⲥⲉⲉⲡⲉ 'remainder, rest'). Functions as 'the remaining ones, the rest' of the catechumens not covered by the present pearl/fruit parables.
